plan.notes: Source: official College of Southern Idaho 2024-2025 catalog, 'Engineering, Associate of Science' program page (Major Code: 1710S), hand-transcribed 2026-10-02 from https://csi.smartcatalogiq.com/en/2024-2025/catalog/engineering-physical-and-computer-sciences-department/engineering/engineering-associate-of-science . Transcription method: fetched the official program page and transcribed the four semester tables verbatim (course codes, titles, credits, printed semester totals 15/17/14/15). TRUE award: Associate of Science (page title). Catalog year 2024-2025: the newest CSI catalog with complete published program pages found (a 2025-2026 catalog exists but its program pages were not locatable; the 2024-2025 pages are complete and officially published). Total credits: 61, the catalog's published total ('Total Credit Hours: 61'); semester tables sum 15+17+14+15 = 61. Choice slots: (a) Fall Sophomore lists 'ECON 202 Principles of Microeconomics OR ECON 201 Principles of Macroeconomics' (both 3 credits) - modeled as one 3-credit choice slot. (b) WELL GE / COMM GE / SOCS GE2 / HUMA GE2 are official catalog placeholders for 'any Gen. Ed.' course in that category (student choice). (c) PROG ELEC rows are 'Program Elective(s)' (student choice: 5 credits in semester 3, 3 credits in semester 4) selected from the emphasis-area elective lists printed on the page (Agricultural, Biological, Chemical, Civil, Computer, Electrical, Mechanical Engineering). Zero-credit coreq labs: 'CHEM 111L General Chemistry 1 Lab* 0 Credits' and 'PHYS 211L Physic Scientists & Engineers 1 Lab* 0 Credit' are official 0-credit corequisite labs, modeled with required_zero:true (excluded from credit sums; semester totals still match the printed 15/17). Prereqs: left empty. The catalog marks courses with '*' as 'Prerequisite or Corequisite required' but does not name the prerequisite on the plan page; per-course prerequisites live on the official catalog course pages, not the plan page. The catalog notes 'Alternative plans of study available by contacting your advisor.'
